requirement_text: There are two ways to apply to Caltech.
source_authority_note: admissions.caltech.edu is a subdomain of caltech.edu and ends in .edu, so it passes looksOfficial() directly -- unlike MIT's separate mitadmissions.org, no ADDITIONAL_OFFICIAL_DOMAINS entry is needed. Confirmed by direct browser navigation before researching, not assumed from the name alone.
researcher_notes: The two paths are the Common App and the QuestBridge Application (see CAL0002). No explicit page-footer update timestamp was found on this page; currency is inferred from the fact that the site's Standardized Tests and Supplemental Essays pages (CAL0016, CAL0018) both explicitly say 'Fall 2027' in their own body text, and this Application Requirements page links to and is structurally part of the same first-year-applicants section.

requirement_text: Common App or QuestBridge Application
researcher_notes: Listed as a checklist item under 'Application materials' alongside the fee (CAL0003), recommendations (CAL0004), and academic materials (CAL0005-0008).

requirement_text: $85 application fee or fee waiver
researcher_notes: Fee-waiver mechanism not detailed on this specific page (unlike Stanford's dedicated fee-waiver page); not fabricated here, left as a gap for a follow-up pass rather than guessed at.

requirement_text: 1 STEM: Calculus (or beyond), Chemistry, Physics, or Biology
researcher_notes: One of two required teacher recommendations, listed under 'Letters of Recommendation' on the same page. Companion record CAL0005 is the second, non-STEM letter -- both required, not alternatives.

requirement_text: 1 Humanities or Social Sciences: English, History, Government, or Economics
researcher_notes: Companion to CAL0004: together, two teacher recommendations are required, one STEM-subject and one Humanities/Social-Sciences-subject, not a free choice of any two teachers.

requirement_text: School Report: This is a document that your high school college counselor will send to Caltech that provides context about your school. You can request your counselor complete it through either application platform.
researcher_notes: Page also notes the counselor can separately submit a letter of recommendation on the applicant's behalf, distinct from this School Report document.

requirement_text: Official transcripts from your secondary school (grades 9-11, or the international curriculum equivalent). Transcripts must be submitted by a school official.
researcher_notes: Grades 9-11 only at initial application, not 9-12 (contrast Stanford's REQ-STA0027, also 9-12) -- senior-year grades arrive separately via the Mid-Year Report (CAL0009). Page also notes applicants cannot submit their own copy; unofficial transcripts may be uploaded initially but official ones are required if admitted and enrolling.

requirement_text: If you have taken college classes while in high school, please provide the college transcript, as well.
researcher_notes: Conditional on having taken dual-enrollment/college coursework; not a universal requirement.

requirement_text: Mid-Year Report (due when first term senior grades are available at your school).
researcher_notes: No fixed calendar date given on this page (contrast Stanford's fixed Feb 15 date) -- tied instead to when the applicant's own school issues first-term senior grades, which varies by school calendar.

requirement_text: We require either the SAT or ACT test scores.
researcher_notes: Restated in more detail, with an explicit fall-2027 cycle qualifier, on the dedicated Standardized Tests page -- see CAL0016/CAL0017. Caltech is test-required, not test-optional, as of this pass -- checked specifically for a stale test-optional statement (per this corpus's own diligence convention) and found none on either page.

requirement_text: If you have taken AP or IB examinations, you will be asked to submit those scores as well.
researcher_notes: Conditional on having taken AP/IB exams; distinct from the specific AP/IB substitution-exam policy for calculus/chemistry/physics course requirements (CAL0015), which is a stricter, separate use of AP/IB scores.

requirement_text: Caltech defines an international applicant as a student who is neither a US citizen nor a permanent resident and who has attended secondary school outside of the United States.
researcher_notes: Governs which applicants CAL0013-0015 below apply to -- defined by school location, not citizenship alone (a US citizen who attended secondary school abroad would not meet this definition; a non-citizen who attended US secondary school would not either).

requirement_text: English Proficiency Exam scores: Required of all international applicants unless 1) your native language is English or 2) English is the primary language of instruction in your secondary school. For non-Native English speakers where English is the primary language of instruction in your secondary school, Caltech strongly recommends an English Proficiency Exam score. We accept the Duolingo English Test (DET), IELTS, or the TOEFL.
researcher_notes: No minimum score threshold stated on this page for DET/IELTS/TOEFL -- not fabricated here. The exam must be taken prior to the application deadline (stated on the same page, not repeated as its own record since it is a scheduling constraint on this same requirement rather than a separate fact).

requirement_text: Caltech is need-aware for international applicants because the total amount of financial aid funds is limited for these students, and we remain committed to meeting the demonstrated need of all admitted students.
researcher_notes: Explicit, unambiguous need-aware policy for international applicants -- same substantive policy shape as Stanford's REQ-STA0011, phrased by the page as 'the application prompts questions to confirm their understanding of our financial aid policy and thus confirm their financial aid intent towards Caltech.' Not need-blind for this population.

requirement_text: Translation of documents: All application materials must be submitted in English. If they were originally printed in a language other than English, we require the original document and an English translation. We will not review your application if any part is not translated in English.
researcher_notes: Hard exclusion, stated in the page's own words ('will not review'), not a soft preference -- same shape as Stanford's REQ-STA0009, though Stanford's page additionally names who may not perform the translation (the applicant) and this page does not specify that detail.

requirement_text: Upon admission, Caltech reserves the right to conduct verifications of submitted proofs. Any discrepancies or falsifications will result in the rescission of your admission to Caltech.
researcher_notes: A standing policy statement (verification/integrity), not a checklist item a student completes -- recorded per this corpus's own convention of capturing named binding-consequence statements as their own row rather than summarizing them away.

requirement_text: To prepare for core, students must demonstrate mastery in the following subjects: Four years of math, including one year of calculus. One year of physics. One year of chemistry. One year of biology (recommended). Four years of English. Two years of history and/or social sciences courses (3+ years recommended).
researcher_notes: Unlike Stanford (REQ-STA0019-0024, explicitly 'recommendations, not requirements'), Caltech's page frames calculus/chemistry/physics/English/history as mandatory ('must demonstrate mastery'), with biology and the extra history/social-science year specifically marked '(recommended)' as the sole soft items in an otherwise required list. This is a genuine, substantive difference between the two institutions' policies, not a research inconsistency.

requirement_text: If a student is unable to take a calculus, chemistry, and/or physics course in high school because it is not available to them or they experience unresolvable course conflicts, Caltech will accept examination scores or the course challenge through Schoolhouse.world showing evidence of knowledge in the subject in lieu of an academic course requirement, provided both the student and their counselor document the underlying unresolvable issue(s).
researcher_notes: The substitution mechanism itself; the specific accepted exams/scores are CAL0019. Gated on documented unavailability/conflict, not freely available to any applicant who simply prefers not to take the course.

requirement_text: A score of 5 on AP exams in AP Calculus AB, AP Calculus BC, AP Chemistry, AP Physics 1, AP Physics 2, or AP Physics C. The AP exam must be taken by application deadline. A score of 6 or 7 on the IB Mathematics HL; Chemistry SL or HL; or Physics SL or HL examinations. The IB exam must be taken by application deadline. Completing the course challenge from Schoolhouse.world in one of the following courses: AP/College Calculus BC; AP/College Chemistry; AP/College Physics 1. Proof of certification from Schoolhouse.world is required within one week of the application deadline.
limitations: Page states this policy 'For in-coming fall 2026 first-year applicants' and 'There will be no exceptions' -- literally quoted and cycle_year set to 2026 to match. No fall-2027-specific version of this exact page was found; whether the same substitution list carries forward to fall 2027 applicants is not directly confirmed by this page and should be re-checked before treating it as settled for the corpus's primary current-cycle assumption (cycle_year 2027, per CAL0020/CAL0022 and this corpus's own convention). Not recorded in the scale_ambiguity field: that field's recognized values are specifically about test-score-scale issues (the TOEFL-rescale shape elsewhere in this corpus), and this is a different kind of doubt -- which future cycle a policy extends to, not whether a score is satisfiable -- so it is left here in prose rather than risk it being misread as the former by a future pass.
researcher_notes: IB thresholds (6 or 7) are notably stricter than typical Caltech course-credit IB policies elsewhere (often 6+ for HL credit) in that only the top two bands qualify here, and this is a substitution-for-a-requirement standard, not a credit-award standard -- do not conflate the two if cross-referencing other Caltech AP/IB credit documentation later.

requirement_text: Caltech requires first-year applicants to submit either the SAT or the ACT for admissions to Caltech. For fall 2027 applicants, Caltech does not require the ACT writing or science subscores. In fairness, Caltech will not consider a student's composite score and instead, Caltech will consider each individual subscore: Math, English, Reading, Science (optional), and Writing (optional).
researcher_notes: Explicitly cycle-labeled 'fall 2027 applicants' in the page's own text, unlike the academic-requirements page (CAL0019), which is why this record is cycle_year 2027 with high confidence while CAL0019 is flagged as an open question. Caltech evaluates individual SAT/ACT subscores, not a composite, which matters for how a future evaluator function should compare this against a single composite-score threshold from another institution's requirement.

requirement_text: SAT (Math or Reading & Writing): Bucket A 780-800, Bucket B 750-770, Bucket C Below 750. ACT (Individual subscore): Bucket A 35-36, Bucket B 33-34, Bucket C Below 33. If your score falls in Bucket A or B, the admissions committee will not see whether you scored a 750 or 800 SAT (33-36 ACT), they will just know you're in a range. If your score falls below a 750 SAT or 33 ACT (Bucket C), the individual exam score will be shown to admissions committee.
researcher_notes: Reconstructed from the page's own table plus its surrounding explanatory prose (both quoted, table cells combined into prose form for JSONL storage; no numbers altered or added). This is not a minimum-score threshold in the pass/fail sense evaluate.ts uses elsewhere -- below Bucket C there is no stated floor, and even a Bucket C score is still reviewed holistically, not auto-rejected. Should not be represented as a simple minimum_grade-style cutoff by a future ingestion pass.

requirement_text: If you had to choose an area of interest or two today, what would you choose? Why did you choose your proposed area of interest? If you selected 'other', what topics are you interested in pursuing? (Min: 150 / Max: 200 words)
researcher_notes: Page header explicitly states 'Fall 2027 Supplemental Application Essays' and that essay prompts 'change annually, are updated, and published in the summer' -- so cycle_year 2027 is directly stated, not inferred, and this exact prompt text should not be assumed to hold for a future cycle without re-checking.

requirement_text: Scholarly Character: How do you learn when there is no easy answer? Choose one of the following prompts: (Max: 200 words) Option 1 -- COLLABORATION: STEM as shared learning; or Option 2 -- PROCESS: The thought behind the outcome.
limitations: Full prompt text for each of the two options is longer than reproduced here; option titles and the choose-one/word-limit structure are exact, full option bodies trimmed for record length -- see source_url for complete wording before this is treated as the full prompt shown to a student.
researcher_notes: One of two 'Required Short Essay Questions' (the other is CAL0024, Scientific Drive) -- both required, this is not an either/or between the two named questions, only within each question's own listed prompt options.

requirement_text: Scientific Drive: How does STEM come alive in your life through learning, pursuing, or making? Choose two of the following prompts: (Two Essays, Max: 200 words each) Option 1 -- LEARNING: STEM as a never-ending rabbit hole; Option 2 -- PURSUING: STEM as sustained intellectual engagement; Option 3 -- MAKING: STEM as creation.
limitations: Full prompt text for each of the three options is longer than reproduced here; option titles and the choose-two/word-limit structure are exact, full option bodies trimmed for record length -- see source_url for complete wording.
researcher_notes: Requires two full essays (200 words each) chosen from three named options, making this the longest single component of Caltech's supplement -- distinct from Scholarly Character (CAL0023), which requires only one.

requirement_text: Caltech students bring more than academic ability to the communities they join. What is something you would be excited to do, share, teach, make, start, or contribute as part of the Caltech community? (Min: 100 / Max: 150 words)
researcher_notes: Labeled 'Fun Question' on the page -- the one required essay prompt not explicitly STEM-framed, unlike CAL0022-0024.

requirement_text: Caltech cares about context. Is there anything about your academic preparation, coursework, school context, or learning experiences that would help us better understand your readiness for Caltech?
limitations: No word-count range visible in the extracted page text for this specific question, unlike CAL0022/CAL0025/CAL0026 -- not fabricated here; left absent rather than guessed.
researcher_notes: Labeled 'Optional Academic Short Answer Question' -- the one essay prompt on this page that is explicitly optional rather than required, distinct from CAL0022-0025.

requirement_text: All Fall 2027 applicants will be asked to review Caltech's guidelines on the ethical use of AI before submitting their supplemental essays.
limitations: The AI-ethics guidelines themselves live on a linked sub-page (ethical-use-of-ai-guidelines-for-fall-applicants) that was not separately fetched this pass -- this record captures only that the review is mandatory before essay submission, not the guidelines' own content.
researcher_notes: A dedicated, named AI-usage policy tied specifically to the current application cycle -- worth flagging as a genuinely new category of admissions requirement neither the Stanford nor the prior MIT-blocked research batches in this corpus recorded, not something this lane invented a category for.
